title: From Selkies to Demons: 7 YA Picks for Paranormal Fans
excerpt: Supernatural creatures take center stage in these thrilling YA stories, including the latest from K. Ancrum, Trang Thanh Tran, and S. Hati.
content:
Supernatural creatures take center stage in these thrilling YA stories, including the latest from K. Ancrum, Trang Thanh Tran, and S. Hati.

Cold, Elias. Selkies & Skeptics. 320p. Page Street YA. Nov. 2026. Tr $22.99. ISBN 9798890034960.
Gr 6 Up–Luella, 16, leads an isolated life. Her controlling father, an alcoholic lighthouse keeper, causes ships to crash by extinguishing the light, then forces Luella to dive for valuables. Luella wants to believe her long-gone mother is a selkie living among the seals that accompany her dives but has no proof. On a whim, she invites the Society for the Protection of Faeries to investigate her (false) claims of selkie sightings. Convincing them that the selkies are real, Luella escapes the island and begins working with the Society members: inquisitive Enoch, skeptical Winifred, and zoophile Ursula. As Luella works alongside her new companions, she struggles with the fear her lies will be discovered as well as lingering questions about her possible fae heritage. A side plot involves locating Enoch’s mother, a fae researcher who disappeared four years ago. Although the Society encounters a rivalry with competing fae researchers, this conflict isn’t as developed as Luella’s inner struggles. Similarly, secondary character development is light, keeping the focus on Luella. Her first-person narration is melancholy, with her negative self-talk lending a morose tone. Occasionally the author tells, rather than shows, the action. The prose is lush, with strong imagery of the setting, reminiscent of 19th-century Britain. Most characters read white; Ursula has dark brown skin and dark hair. Enoch is trans. Luella is partially deaf from an injury sustained while diving. VERDICT Purchase where historical fantasy is popular.–Hannah Grasse

Ancrum, K. Ellie Ellie. 384p. Holt. Jan. 2027. Tr $20.99. ISBN 9781250265272.
Gr 9 Up–High school senior Ellie is counting the days until graduation when she can leave her impoverished small town. But a series of poor decisions puts her in the path of a dangerous shape-shifting creature—one who shares her face. A tentative friendship begins to form as they learn that a face is not the only thing they have in common. Each of their lives features things more dangerous to them than each other, and these things threaten to break their budding relationship. The darkness in this story comes from the situations that Ellie and the creature face rather than any supernatural danger, which makes this coming-of-age story a good choice for readers who appreciate a slow burn. An undercurrent of tension is present throughout the first half as Ellie struggles to reconcile her resentment toward her careless guardian and learns of her new friend’s powers and their dark past. An explosive midpoint gives a turn toward more mature themes, including domestic violence, and leads to a satisfying conclusion. Readers familiar with Ancrum’s previous works, notably Icarus and The Corruption of Hollis Brown, will recognize similar themes of connection as well as her signature blend of the mystical and stark realism. Ellie is Black; her guardian is white; and the shapeshifter appears as Black, Asian, Latine, and white at different points. VERDICT Fans of Ancrum’s previous work will find much to enjoy in this story, as will any teen who appreciates a creeping horror with real-life themes.–Mimi Powell

Hati, S. What Haunts the Ice. 368p. Feiwel & Friends. Jan. 2027. Tr $20.99. ISBN 9781250392848.
Gr 9 Up–Hati’s novel throws readers into an ice-cold paranormal adventure. During a trek to Antarctica, a diverse group of teenagers is suddenly thrust into a bone-chilling hunt for the truth after the mysterious and sudden death of one of their guides, followed by ghostly sightings. The group of newly minted friends must balance their sanity, friendship, and safety to discover what is going on with the strange apparitions that keep showing up and determine if these apparitions are out for blood. Readers will find the two female narrators, Zoe and Payal, personable and realistic, but may struggle to separate their voices when going from chapter to chapter as the narration style does not vary. Well-crafted secondary characters range from endearing to enraging and come from all over the world. VERDICT A good addition to libraries in need of a paranormal adventure set in a mysterious place.–Harley Smith

Jasinska, Alicia. This Lethal Love. 448p. (Spirits and Saints: Bk. 2). Peachtree Teen. Jan. 2027. Tr $21.99. ISBN 9781682638699.
Gr 9 Up–In the expansive sequel to This ­Fatal Kiss, a Slavic reimagining of “The ­Little Mermaid,” the world of demons, spirits, magical objects, and complicated relationships grows and deepens. Readers return to the trio of protagonists: Gisela, a former rusałka (water nymph), now human and alive once again; Aleksey, a bies (forest demon) possessing the body of a human boy; and Kazik, the exorcist who finds himself romantically entangled with both. This installment retains the flirty banter, nuanced queer representation, and diverse range of spirits and demons from Slavic folklore that set its predecessor apart from other teen romantasies. This book deftly handles the developing polyamorous relationship among the three teens as they stumble through moments of jealousy and insecurity together. Past secrets, new magical powers, and rivaling demons fill the novel with plenty of action, although the plot suffers slightly from a lack of focus amid so many new characters and schemes. However, the short chapters and rotating points of view keep the pace moving, and the snappy ­dialogue is as charming as ever. VERDICT Fans of This Fatal Kiss will be thrilled to return to the chaotic and fascinating world where Slavic folklore meets the animated fantasy film Spirited Away.–Molly Saunders

Le, Vanessa. When Shadows Burn. 384p. (When Shadows Burn: Bk. 1). Holt. Dec. 2026. Tr $22.99. ISBN 9781250420473.
Gr 8 Up–An unlikely pair hunts a dangerous demon in this dark academia novel tinged with romance and mystery. Song Sarna is the top demon slayer in her class at Phenbridge University, using her blood to create weapons that can capture and kill demons. Kiet Sren is a Phenbridge dropout whose blood attracts demons, allowing him to anchor the demons to his body and make them vulnerable to attack. Together they form Inkspill Agency, an unaccredited demon-hunting business. When a demon they slay is linked to the mysterious organization named the Red Feathers that was responsible for the death of Kiet’s brother years before, the duo races to unravel the Red Feathers’s secrets before there are more victims. Kiet and Song face incredible danger as their investigation casts suspicion on powerful players that are inside Phenbridge University. Le creates a captivating and unique fantasy world full of demon-slaying lore. The use of blood as a tool and consequently the toll that it takes on Song’s body builds a grisly atmosphere that heightens the stakes of the investigation. Chapters from Song’s and Kiet’s perspectives capture the protagonists’ motivations and fears, building romantic tension without derailing the momentum of the mystery. Song’s and Kiet’s families have roots in the fictional Renisia, which is influenced by elements of Southeast and East Asian culture. VERDICT An exceptional duology opener.–Emily Yates

Strychacz, Isabel. Thirteen Midnights. 368p. S. & S. Nov. 2026. Tr $21.99. ISBN 9798347101009.
Gr 8 Up–A novel teeming with magic, oral storytelling, intricate character webs, and the power of fate and love. Violet ­Holloway, a white female, has been told stories for as long as she can remember about the monstrous Piper, the Lord of the Woods, and how to protect herself from his otherworld magic. When Violet’s grandmother passes away, Violent knows that as the last in line—the thirteenth ­Holloway—she is destined to kill the Piper and break the curse that has been haunting her family for years. But somehow, both Violet and her best friend, Blair, find themselves stuck in the Piper’s complex labyrinth. As the story unfolds, truths and lies of past and present surface, and Violet is forced to decide where home truly lies. The plot line is intense, mysterious, and highly ­suspenseful as each chapter builds upon the previous one, with flashbacks from the ­Holloway past sprinkled throughout. ­Dialogue ­between characters moves the plot along quickly and reveals layers of secret character traits, feelings, and thoughts. Readers will find Violet resourceful and inquisitive and the Piper to be much different than traditionally portrayed. Though magic is the primary theme, it is the human elements that make the book impossible to put down: readers will become invested in the lives of the characters, and through them understand that there is more to a person than what is seen on the outside. VERDICT A powerful “Beauty and the Beast”–like novel with a “Pied Piper” thread that ­unpacks the challenges of the past while celebrating what could be.–­Brianna Amoscato

Tran, Trang Thanh. The Summoning of Tess Pham. 288p. Bloomsbury YA. Feb. 2027. Tr $20.99. ISBN 9781547619054.
Gr 9 Up–An atmospheric horror with a chilling supernatural narrative. Eighteen-year-old Vietnamese American Tess Pham travels from Washington to Vietnam to scatter the ashes of her recently deceased brother. Tess arrives at her estranged grandmother’s isolated home accompanied by her half sister and her two best friends. There, Tess is thrust into mounting family tensions, unexpected caregiving responsibilities, and a community unraveling ­under the weight of supernatural forces. As the story unfolds over one harrowing night, Tess is forced to confront difficult questions about her family’s past, her complicated ­relationship with Vietnam and the legacy of the war, her love of the traditional lên ng ritual dance, and the shamanic heritage that has shaped generations of her family. Tran skillfully intertwines these personal conflicts with escalating horror, allowing the emotional stakes to deepen alongside the supernatural terror. The family dynamics feel authentic and deeply nuanced, making the horror all the more effective because it grows naturally from the characters’ grief, guilt, and fractured loyalties. The novel also thoughtfully explores what defines family—not simply blood ties but love, responsibility, and shared history. The cast is predominantly Vietnamese. Tess and her sister are queer. VERDICT Tran’s fans will find much to appreciate here, particularly the blend of psychological tension, cultural folklore, and visceral horror. Readers who enjoyed Jill Baguchinsky’s May the Dead Keep You or Romina ­Garber’s Castle of the Cursed will likewise find this haunting, emotionally resonant novel well worth reading.–Susan Catlett
